definitions.explanation: Items offered to deities, spirits of the deceased, or at Buddhist altars. Typically includes food, drink, flowers, and other items placed at shrines, temples, graves, or household altars.

examples.japanese: {仏壇|ぶつだん}にお{供|そな}え{物|もの}を{置|お}いた。
examples.english: I placed an offering on the Buddhist altar.

examples.japanese: お{供|そな}え{物|もの}に{果物|くだもの}とお{菓子|かし}を{用意|ようい}した。
examples.english: I prepared fruit and sweets as offerings.

examples.japanese: お{正月|しょうがつ}には{神棚|かみだな}にお{供|そな}え{物|もの}をして、{新|あたら}しい{年|とし}の{無事|ぶじ}を{祈|いの}る。
examples.english: At New Year's, we place offerings on the household shrine and pray for a safe year ahead.

notes:
CULTURE:
お{供|そな}え{物|もの} is central to Japanese religious practice. Common offerings include {米|こめ} (rice), {酒|さけ} (sake), {果物|くだもの} (fruit), お{菓子|かし} (sweets), and {花|はな} (flowers). After the offering period, food items are often consumed by the family, a practice called お{下|さ}がり.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{供|そな}え{物|もの}をする (to make an offering)
- お{供|そな}え{物|もの}を{上|あ}げる (to offer up)
- お{供|そな}え{物|もの}を{下|さ}げる (to take down an offering)

FORM:
The plain form {供え物|そなえもの} (without お) also exists but is less common in everyday speech.
